articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi: 500 Million Indians Lifted Out of Poverty
articles.summary: Addressing a gathering in Gujarat, PM Narendra Modi stated that 500 million Indians have emerged from poverty in the last decade, calling it the biggest event since independence. He highlighted the 'Saath-Saath' milan where workers from 182 assembly constituencies participated. Modi credited government policies for creating a new era of prosperity for the downtrodden.

articles.headline: Analysis Claims CPCB AQI Methods Understate Severity of Delhi Pollution
articles.summary: An HT investigation suggests the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) uses calculation methods that suppress the true severity of Delhi's air pollution. By using 24-hour averages that flatten peak levels, many 'severe' air days are reported as 'very poor.' Official data for Nov 9 showed an AQI of 344, while hourly data across 47 stations suggested a true average of 411.

articles.headline: ED Seeks Extradition of Two More Accused in Mahadev Betting Case
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has moved to extradite Kumar Agarwal and another key operative from the UAE in connection with the ₹6,000 crore Mahadev online betting fraud. The agency is already pursuing the extradition of co-founders Ravi Uppal and Saurabh Chandrakar. The accused are alleged to have managed a syndicate of call centers and betting websites across several countries.

articles.headline: Two Army Personnel Killed by Tank During Training Exercise in Hisar
articles.summary: Lance Naik Manish Kumar and Naik Manish Kumar were killed during a routine military exercise in Hisar, Haryana, when they were accidentally run over by a tank. Police stated that heavy dust clouds during the maneuvers may have obscured the driver's vision. An FIR has been registered under Section 194 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and investigations are ongoing.

articles.headline: Maharashtra to Replace Tribal Welfare Cash Transfers With Digital Rupee
articles.summary: The Maharashtra government plans to replace direct bank transfers for tribal welfare schemes with a digital rupee system starting April 1, 2027. Under the new guidelines, benefits will be credited to digital wallets and can only be used at registered vendors. The move is aimed at curbing corruption and ensuring funds are spent on intended items like food and education.

articles.headline: MCD Bans Lodging Above Third Floor in New Guest House Norms
articles.summary: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has issued strict fire safety guidelines banning commercial lodging activities on the fourth floor or above in guest houses. The order follows a fatal fire in Hauz Rani. Buildings taller than 12 metres must now obtain a Fire No-Objection Certificate (NOC). MCD has launched a month-long drive to ensure compliance with these safety standards.

articles.headline: Tata Sons Schedules EGM Proposal for November 26 Board Meeting
articles.summary: Tata Sons has included a proposal to convene a Special General Meeting (EGM) on the agenda for its November 26 board meeting. The move comes amid reports of internal discussions regarding the company's governance and leadership structure. The board will also discuss the conglomerate's financial performance and future investment plans for its various business verticals.

articles.headline: India and Netherlands Discuss Plan for Ukraine Ceasefire Negotiations
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met his Dutch counterpart Caspar Veldkamp to review bilateral ties and discuss a potential framework for a ceasefire in Ukraine. The meeting highlighted India's growing role as a mediator in global conflicts. Both nations also agreed to strengthen cooperation in semiconductors, maritime security, and green energy sectors.

articles.headline: Seven Killed as Car Collides With Truck in Gujarat's Kutch
articles.summary: Seven people, including two Army personnel, were killed after their car collided head-on with a truck on the Bhuj-Khavda highway in Gujarat's Kutch district. The victims, from two families, were returning from a visit to the Rann of Kutch. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Droupadi Murmu expressed grief over the incident and announced ex-gratia for the families.

articles.headline: Gukesh Aiming for Win Not Just Defense in Chess Championship
articles.summary: Indian Grandmaster D. Gukesh, ahead of his World Chess Championship match against Ding Liren, stated he is playing to win the title rather than just defending his position. The 18-year-old challenger highlighted his intense preparation and mental focus. The match, starting in Singapore, is seen as a historic opportunity for India to regain the world title.

articles.headline: US Investigating Nvidia Over Sale of Advanced AI Chips to China
articles.summary: The US Department of Commerce is questioning Nvidia regarding reports that its advanced AI chips reached Chinese firms despite export bans. Investigators are looking into potential sanctions violations through third-party distributors in Singapore and elsewhere. Nvidia has stated it complies with all US regulations and is cooperating with the ongoing federal inquiry.

articles.headline: Marc Marquez Wins Eighth MotoGP Title Following Portuguese Grand Prix
articles.summary: Spanish rider Marc Marquez secured his eighth MotoGP world championship title after finishing eighth in the season-ending Portuguese Grand Prix. Marquez maintained a sufficient points lead over rival Jorge Martin to claim the crown. The victory marks a significant comeback for Marquez after seasons hampered by injury, cementing his status as one of the sport's greatest competitors.

articles.headline: Indian Navy Officers Show Little Interest in New Traditional Mess Attire
articles.summary: A new dress code introduced by the Indian Navy in February 2024, featuring traditional Indian attire like kurta-pyjamas for officers' messes, has reportedly found few takers. Despite efforts to 'decolonize' military traditions, most officers still prefer the conventional shirt-and-trouser combination. Naval authorities noted that while the option exists, voluntary adoption remains low.

articles.headline: Delhi Police Hunt for SUV Driver in Fatal Kashmere Gate Crash
articles.summary: Police have launched a manhunt for the driver of a luxury SUV that rammed into an auto-rickshaw and pedestrians near Kashmere Gate, killing two people. The suspect was initially apprehended but was later released on bail before the victims succumbed to their injuries. Authorities have now upgraded the charges to culpable homicide and are conducting raids across the NCR.

articles.headline: Delhi High Court to Hear Pleas Regarding Krishi Bhawan Mosque Today
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court is scheduled to hear petitions today concerning the preservation of a century-old mosque located within the Krishi Bhawan complex. The petitioners are seeking protection against potential demolition as part of the Central Vista redevelopment project. The court had previously sought responses from the Centre and local authorities regarding the heritage status of the structure.

articles.headline: Delhi Falls Short on Key Infrastructure Targets for Pollution Control
articles.summary: A report by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) reveals that Delhi has missed several key infrastructure targets aimed at curbing air pollution. Shortfalls were noted in the installation of continuous ambient air quality monitoring stations and the deployment of e-buses. While some targets for waste management were met, the lag in transport infra remains a concern.

articles.headline: Delhi Police Rescue Kidnapped Eight Month Old Baby From Aligarh
articles.summary: Delhi Police successfully rescued an eight-month-old infant who was kidnapped from the Mandawali area and arrested three suspects, including a woman. The child was traced to Aligarh in Uttar Pradesh using CCTV footage and technical surveillance. Investigators believe the kidnapping was carried out with the intention of selling the child to a childless couple.

articles.headline: Delhi Jal Board Plans to Monetise Five Properties for Infrastructure Fund
articles.summary: The Delhi Jal Board (DJB) has identified five prime properties across the city for monetization to raise funds for its water and sewage infrastructure revamp. The board plans to lease these assets for commercial and residential development. The revenue generated will be used to clear pending bills and fund long-term projects aimed at improving the city's water supply network.

articles.headline: Pakistan Minister Calls for Joint Forum to Address Terrorism Concerns
articles.summary: Pakistan's Minister for Information and Broadcasting, Musadik Malik, suggested that India and Pakistan should create a joint forum to discuss and address terrorism-related evidence and concerns. Speaking on the sidelines of a regional summit, Malik emphasized that dialogue is the only way to resolve long-standing disputes and build regional stability.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi Claims BJP and RSS Lack Understanding of Indian Traditions
articles.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi criticized the BJP and RSS, alleging they have a superficial and distorted understanding of India's spiritual and cultural traditions. Speaking at a book launch, Gandhi argued that the ruling party uses religion for political gain rather than following true inclusive values. He called for a return to a more pluralistic and compassionate vision of India.

articles.headline: Toll From Spurious Liquor Consumption in Manipur Rises to 18
articles.summary: The death toll from the consumption of suspected spurious liquor in Manipur's Chandel and Kakching districts has risen to 18. Several others remain hospitalized in critical condition. State authorities have suspended local police officials for negligence and launched a crackdown on illegal liquor dens. A high-level committee has been formed to investigate the source of the toxic alcohol.

articles.headline: Financing Hurdles Stall Adoption of Electric Buses and Heavy Trucks
articles.summary: A new report suggests that high interest rates and lack of standardized residual value assessments are stalling the adoption of electric buses and trucks in India. Despite government subsidies, private operators are struggling to secure affordable loans for fleet conversion. Experts suggest the creation of a specialized green finance body to mitigate risks for lenders and borrowers.

articles.headline: Government to Prepare Monthly Sugar Output Estimates for Next Season
articles.summary: The Union Ministry of Consumer Affairs has announced plans to prepare monthly sugar production estimates for the 2026-27 season to ensure better price stability. The move aims to provide more accurate data on stocks and consumption, helping the government make timely decisions on export and import quotas. Industry bodies have welcomed the step as a move toward greater transparency.

articles.headline: Hyderabad on High Alert Following Bomb Threat Email to Police
articles.summary: Security has been beefed up across Hyderabad after the city police received an email threatening bomb blasts at prominent locations, including IT parks and shopping malls. Special teams have been formed to trace the origin of the email. While initial checks at several sites found no suspicious objects, authorities have advised citizens to remain vigilant and report any unusual activity.

articles.headline: Chief Justice: Criticise Decisions Not Institutions at University Convocation
articles.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Sanjiv Khanna, while addressing students at Himachal Pradesh University, stated that while citizens have the right to criticize court judgments, they should avoid attacking the institutions themselves. He emphasized that the judiciary's role is to uphold the Constitution and that maintaining public trust in the system is essential for a healthy democracy.

articles.headline: Vladimir Putin Praises India's Ancient Civilisation and Cultural Diversity
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin praised India as a great power with a rich ancient civilization and remarkable cultural diversity. In an interview, Putin highlighted the long-standing strategic partnership between Moscow and New Delhi, noting that India's independent foreign policy is a pillar of the multipolar world. He also expressed interest in expanding trade and energy cooperation.

articles.headline: South Korea Education Chief Resigns Over AI Assisted Cheating Scandal
articles.summary: South Korea's Education Minister has resigned following a major scandal involving the use of AI-powered devices for cheating in national exams. The scandal broke after dozens of students were found using hidden gadgets to access AI chatbots during a high-stakes university entrance test. The government has announced a total overhaul of exam hall security and a ban on all digital devices.

articles.headline: RBI maintains repo rate at 6.5 percent amid inflation concerns
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee has decided to keep the repo rate unchanged at 6.5%. Governor Shaktikanta Das cited the need to align inflation with the 4% target while supporting economic growth. The decision follows a three-day review, maintaining a 'withdrawal of accommodation' stance to ensure price stability remains a priority for the central bank.

articles.headline: India's GDP growth projected at 7.3 percent for fiscal year
articles.summary: The National Statistical Office (NSO) has released advance estimates projecting India's real GDP growth at 7.3% for the current financial year. Growth is driven by strong performance in manufacturing and construction. The government attributes this resilience to robust domestic demand and increased public capital expenditure, despite ongoing global geopolitical uncertainties.

articles.headline: Retail inflation eases to 5.1 percent as food prices soften
articles.summary: Consumer Price Index (CPI) data shows retail inflation softened to 5.1% last month, down from 5.7% in the previous period. The decline was primarily attributed to lower vegetable prices and a reduction in domestic fuel costs. While core inflation remains stable, economists suggest the central bank will keep rates high until inflation consistently aligns with long-term targets.

articles.headline: Sensex gains 400 points as banking stocks lead market rally
articles.summary: The BSE Sensex surged 400 points to close at a new record high, led by gains in HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank. Positive global cues and steady foreign institutional investment (FII) inflows boosted investor sentiment. The Nifty 50 also crossed the 22,000 mark for the first time, reflecting broad-based buying across mid-cap and small-cap indices in the Indian markets.

articles.headline: Sebi introduces stricter disclosure norms for high-risk offshore funds
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has mandated additional disclosures for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) holding concentrated stakes in single corporate groups. The new rules aim to prevent potential circumvention of Minimum Public Shareholding requirements. Funds exceeding specific threshold limits must now provide granular details of their ultimate beneficial owners.

articles.headline: Finance Ministry reports record GST collections of 1.70 lakh crore
articles.summary: Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections reached ₹1.70 lakh crore this month, marking a 10% year-on-year growth. This represents the third-highest monthly collection ever recorded. The Finance Ministry attributed the rise to improved taxpayer compliance, increased domestic consumption, and stringent measures against tax evasion and fraudulent input tax credit claims.

articles.headline: Government increases minimum support price for key winter crops
articles.summary: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has approved an increase in the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for all mandated Rabi crops for the 2024-25 marketing season. The move aims to ensure remunerative prices for farmers and encourage crop diversification. The highest increase was announced for lentils and mustard, aligning with the government's goal of achieving self-sufficiency in oilseeds.

articles.headline: Reliance Industries reports 10 percent rise in quarterly net profit
articles.summary: Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) announced a consolidated net profit increase of 10.3% for the December quarter, reaching ₹17,265 crore. Growth was driven by the retail and telecommunications segments. While the oil-to-chemicals business faced margin pressures due to global oil price volatility, Jio's subscriber growth and increased retail footfall exceeded analyst expectations.

articles.headline: Major IT firms pivot towards AI as traditional software demand slows
articles.summary: Leading Indian IT services firms including TCS and Infosys are shifting focus to Generative AI projects following a slowdown in traditional cloud deals. Companies are retraining thousands of employees in AI technologies to meet evolving client demands in the US and Europe. Management indicates that while discretionary spending is tight, AI-related revenue streams are scaling rapidly.

articles.headline: US Federal Reserve signals potential rate cuts later this year
articles.summary: Federal Reserve officials indicated that interest rates have likely peaked and hinted at multiple rate cuts in 2024. Chairman Jerome Powell stated that while inflation is declining toward the 2% goal, the central bank remains cautious. Global markets reacted positively, with treasury yields softening and equity markets in Asia and Europe gaining momentum on the news.

articles.headline: Government allocates 2.7 lakh crore for national highway development
articles.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has announced a plan to complete 12,000 km of highways this year with a budget of ₹2.7 lakh crore. Focus areas include greenfield expressways and improving connectivity in the Northeast. The initiative aims to reduce logistics costs for the industry and improve the overall speed of freight movement across the country.

articles.headline: BCCI unveils schedule for domestic T20 league starting next month
articles.summary: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has released the schedule for the upcoming domestic T20 tournament. The event will feature 10 teams playing across five venues over six weeks. The tournament serves as a key talent scouting platform for the national team. High-profile international players are also expected to participate as guest players in several franchises.

articles.headline: Supreme Court clarifies IBC provisions regarding homebuyer rights as creditors
articles.summary: In a landmark judgment, the Supreme Court upheld that homebuyers must be treated as financial creditors under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). The ruling ensures that individuals who have invested in real estate projects have a seat on the Committee of Creditors. This decision provides significant legal protection to thousands of victims of stalled housing projects.

articles.headline: Experimental Drugs Show Breakthrough Results for Pancreatic and Leukemia Cancers
articles.summary: Clinical trials for daraxonrasib show a 90% success rate in halting tumor growth for pancreatic cancer. Meanwhile, Sellas Life Sciences reported that its leukemia vaccine, galinpepimut-S, improved overall survival by nine months in phase 3 trials. Experts note these treatments target high-mortality cancers, potentially shifting how pharmaceutical firms allocate oncology research resources.

articles.headline: Reduced Import Tariffs Fuel Sevenfold Growth in Indian Mobile Phone Exports
articles.summary: Trade policy shifts, including lowering duties on camera modules and lens inputs to zero, have significantly boosted India's electronics sector. A report by the Foundation for Economic Development shows mobile exports grew sevenfold and jobs tripled between 2022 and 2026. The study suggests similar tariff reforms in engineering sectors could create four million additional jobs.

articles.headline: Tata Sons Board to Discuss EGM Proposals Amid Internal Quorum Challenges
articles.summary: Tata Sons directors will meet Thursday to discuss convening an extraordinary general meeting (EGM) despite lacking the required quorum. The agenda includes Noel Tata’s objections to Chairman N Chandrasekaran’s third term and potential public listing plans. Current legal restrictions prevent Sir Ratan Tata Trusts from sending representatives, leaving the EGM quorum in limbo.

articles.headline: Sebi Proposes 12-Year Cap for Stock Exchange MDs to Mitigate Risks
articles.summary: A new Sebi consultation paper suggests limiting the total tenure of managing directors at market infrastructure institutions to 12 years. If implemented, NSE MD Ashishkumar Chauhan may step down by July 2027. Conversely, BSE MD Sundararaman Ramamurthy could extend his term beyond the current retirement age of 65. The proposal aims to prevent keyman risk and institutional entrenchment.

articles.headline: Ola Electric Struggles with Battery Production Yields at New Gigafactory
articles.summary: Ola Electric’s battery cell manufacturing plant is facing challenges in meeting production targets and quality yields. Two senior executives have departed as the firm struggles to lift cell yields from 70-75% to the commercially viable 90% benchmark. The company plans to shift 70% of its scooter portfolio to LFP batteries, making manufacturing improvements critical for profitability.

articles.headline: Tech Institutes Launch High-Fee Bootcamps to Train AI Forward-Deployed Engineers
articles.summary: New coaching institutes are charging up to ₹4 lakh for 10-month courses to train 'forward-deployed engineers' (FDEs). These specialists combine AI technical skills with sales and consulting for large tech services firms. Demand is surging as companies like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro plan to hire thousands of FDEs to manage AI-led software development and automated agentic workflows.

articles.headline: Centre Offers Incentives to Help Discoms Manage Rising Rooftop Solar Energy
articles.summary: The Union ministry of new and renewable energy will provide ₹2 crore per utility to 15 discoms to adopt smart grid management software. The funding aims to maintain grid stability as decentralized renewable energy, like the 20GW of solar installed under the PM Suryaghar scheme, causes voltage fluctuations. Selected utilities must deploy the Derms software within six months.

articles.headline: CII Proposes Major Financial Reforms for $26.5 Trillion Economy Goal
articles.summary: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) has recommended sweeping reforms across banking, NBFCs, and capital markets to reach a $26.5 trillion economy by 2047. Key proposals include a permanent liquidity window for well-governed NBFCs and growing banking assets to 1.5 times GDP. The body estimates that total financial assets would need to reach $106 trillion to support this growth.

articles.headline: Rising Protein Prices Strain Household Budgets and National Nutritional Intake
articles.summary: Retail food inflation surged to 8.94% in October, driven by sharp increases in the prices of pulses, eggs, and meat. Arhar dal prices rose 15.33% year-on-year, while egg inflation reached 8.33%. Experts warn that these rising costs are forcing lower-income families to compromise on nutrition as animal and plant-based protein sources become increasingly unaffordable.

articles.headline: M1xchange Seeks TReDS Technology Partnerships in Russia and Brazil
articles.summary: M1xchange, India's second-largest invoice discounting platform, is in talks with banks in Russia and Brazil for technology-sharing deals. This follows a Brics agreement to explore common invoice-discounting systems for small businesses. The domestic TReDS market financed invoices worth ₹3.5 trillion in FY26, and the platform is already operational or in talks across several African nations.

articles.headline: Defence Tech Funding Drops to $73 Million as Investors Turn Cautious
articles.summary: Private market funding for Indian defence startups plummeted to $73 million in 2026, down from $304 million in 2025. While seed-stage activity remains, growth-stage deals have stalled as investors demand stronger revenue visibility and conversion of orders into margins. Despite the slowdown, companies like IG Defence and Big Bang Boom Solutions are still seeking fresh capital.

articles.headline: Anthropic's $1.5 Trillion IPO Raises Benchmark for Indian AI Startups
articles.summary: Anthropic’s massive market debut validates the commercial potential of AI but increases pressure on Indian startups to differentiate. Experts suggest Indian firms must focus on vertical AI solutions and 'owning intelligence' rather than just building applications on top of global models. The listing highlights the risk of a 'token tax' where frontier-model providers capture recurring value.

articles.headline: Chinese AI Stocks Lose $1.7 Trillion in Value Since June
articles.summary: China’s AI sector has seen a massive $1.7 trillion wipeout in market value since the end of June 2026. Frothy valuations and tightening US technology export restrictions have fueled the selloff. Investors are increasingly concerned about an AI capital expenditure slowdown and supply chain disruptions, causing tech-focused indexes to shed gains made earlier in the year.

articles.headline: Consumer Watchdog Launches Games and Reels to Engage Gen Z Shoppers
articles.summary: The Department of Consumer Affairs has launched AI games and Instagram Reel challenges to educate young shoppers about their rights. The push comes as annual grievances against e-commerce platforms like Flipkart and Amazon more than doubled since 2021. New rules banning deceptive website designs and hidden charges are also set to take effect from 2027 to protect digital consumers.

articles.headline: Perfetti Van Melle India Eyes ₹4,000 Crore Revenue in 2026
articles.summary: Confectionery maker Perfetti Van Melle is on track to reach ₹4,000 crore in annual revenue, aided by GST rate cuts on candy and chocolate. Managing Director Nikhil Sharma noted that while GST benefits have helped profitability, rising commodity prices and weak rural consumption pose challenges. The firm reported a net profit of ₹230 crore in FY25 on revenue of ₹2,997 crore.

articles.headline: Private Credit Firms Face Delays in Saudi Arabia's $100 Billion Market
articles.summary: Global private credit firms are struggling to deploy capital in Saudi Arabia due to regulatory friction and slow deal structures. Despite an estimated $100 billion opportunity, a recent $150 million financing deal took months to complete. Local regulations and a liquidity crunch exacerbated by regional conflict have slowed the flow of international investment into the kingdom.

articles.headline: Singapore Charges Associate of Alice Huang in Nvidia Chip Smuggling Case
articles.summary: Chinese national Li Ming has been identified as a central operator in a web of companies smuggling restricted Nvidia AI chips to China. Li worked closely with Alice Huang at Megaspeed, a firm that allegedly lied to Nvidia to gain priority access to leading-edge hardware. Singapore authorities have filed fraud charges linked to at least $300 million worth of hardware shipments.

articles.headline: Ukraine Expands Missile Production but Faces Severe Funding and Safety Constraints
articles.summary: Ukraine’s defense industry has rapidly scaled production of Neptune missiles and long-range drones but faces a funding ceiling. Fragmentation across 1,300 companies and constant Russian bombardment of factories are hindering expansion. Industry leaders are now looking to establish Western manufacturing bases and raise foreign capital to compete with Russia's larger production scale.

articles.headline: Restaurant Groups Shift Focus to Delivery and Premium Destination Formats
articles.summary: Rising real estate costs and the growth of food delivery are prompting Indian restaurant groups to launch smaller, delivery-led brands. Companies like Impresario and Azure Hospitality are balancing scalable product-led models with exclusive destination venues. Cloud kitchens are currently growing at 30%, significantly outpacing the 5-10% growth seen in conventional casual dining.

articles.headline: Broadcasters Revive Classic TV Shows to Combat Declining Linear Viewership
articles.summary: JioStar and other networks are bringing back legacy properties like 'Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi' to capitalize on audience nostalgia. This strategy aims to de-risk content in a fragmented market where new shows struggle to build habits. The revival of 'Kyunki' clocked 1.659 billion minutes of watch time in its launch week, showing the enduring power of established content brands.

articles.headline: India and EU Set to Sign Major Free Trade Agreement on 16 December
articles.summary: India and the European Union are expected to sign a comprehensive free trade agreement (FTA) next month. The deal will provide duty-free access for 93% of Indian shipments to the 27-nation bloc. Known as the 'mother of all deals', the agreement will create a unified market of 2 billion people and make luxury imports from the EU, such as cars and wines, significantly cheaper for Indians.

articles.headline: Russian Missile Strike on Apartment Near Kyiv Kills Two People
articles.summary: A Russian missile strike destroyed a five-story apartment building in Dymer, north of the Ukrainian capital, killing at least two people. Rescue teams are working to find nearly a dozen others believed to be trapped under the rubble. The attack comes amid rare air raid alerts in Kaliningrad following reports of drone activity near a major Russian naval base in the Baltic region.

articles.headline: El Niño Strengthening Triggers Food Inflation and Severe Water Shortages in India
articles.summary: A powerful El Niño has caused a 13% monsoon deficit, leading to drought declarations in six Indian states. Food inflation hit 8.9% in October as reservoir levels dropped and winter crop sowing lagged. Major cities like Hyderabad face acute water shortages, with officials declaring emergencies. Experts warn of a polycrisis involving high food prices and record heat-related fatalities in early 2027.

articles.headline: Gold and Silver Prices Plummet as US Fed Maintains Hawkish Stance
articles.summary: Gold and silver ETFs have dropped 30% and 58%, respectively, from their January 2026 peaks. The correction is driven by a stronger US dollar and expectations of continued Fed interest rate hikes through 2027. Rising bond yields have reduced the appeal of non-yielding metals. Analysts advise investors to cap precious metal exposure at 10-15% of their portfolios while buying the dip.

articles.headline: Mahanadi Coalfields Opens ₹8,981 Crore IPO for Market Listing
articles.summary: Mahanadi Coalfields (MCL), India's largest coal producer, has launched its ₹8,981 crore initial public offering. Coal India is selling a 10% stake in the subsidiary at a price band of ₹129-136 per share. The IPO, which values the company at ₹90,010 crore, is entirely an offer for sale. Proceeds will fund Coal India’s diversification into renewable energy and coal gasification.

articles.headline: US GDP and Inflation Data to Shape Federal Reserve's December Policy
articles.summary: Economists are tracking revised US third-quarter GDP figures and October PCE inflation data due on 25 November. Previous estimates put GDP growth at 3.4%, but core inflation remains stubbornly high at 3.1%. The readings will determine whether the Federal Reserve implements a 25 or 50 basis point rate hike in December to contain price pressures without stalling economic activity.

articles.headline: International Film Festival of India to Award Prestigious Golden Peacock
articles.summary: The 57th International Film Festival of India will conclude in Goa on 28 November. A jury has shortlisted 12 films from across the world for the Golden Peacock award for Best Feature Film, which carries a ₹51 lakh prize. This year's festival features over 150 films from 86 countries. Historically, Iran, India, and Russia have led the tally for the top prize since 1965.

articles.headline: Architecture Firm Studio IV Designs Invests in Tier-II Hospitality Growth
articles.summary: Vandana Dhawan Saxena, founder of Studio IV Designs, is focusing on the emotional quotient of architecture in projects across non-metro cities. The firm’s philosophy emphasizes connecting buildings to their local context. Saxena, who advocates for mentorship and disciplined task management, notes that her practice aims to rebuild the relationship between people and their living spaces.

articles.headline: India and Nepal to ink multiple cooperation pacts
articles.summary: Foreign Minister S Jaishankar met Nepal PM Balendra Shah in New Delhi to discuss bilateral ties. The leaders are expected to sign forward-looking agreements in energy, infrastructure, technology, and connectivity. Nepal is also seeking two-way low-altitude air entry corridors and a $2 billion economic aid package from India to support infrastructure and disaster resilience.

articles.headline: ASHA workers continue protest as DKS appeals for patience
articles.summary: The round-the-clock protest by ASHA workers seeking a monthly honorarium of Rs 15,000 entered its second week. Karnataka Deputy CM DK Shivakumar appealed to the health workers to end the agitation, promising a solution in the next cabinet meeting. He cited the involvement of multiple departments for the delay in a final decision regarding their financial demands.

articles.headline: Two soldiers die after tank accident during Haryana drill
articles.summary: Two Indian Army soldiers, Naik Manish Kumar and Naik Ankush Kumar, died after being run over by a tank during a military exercise near Bhojraj village in Haryana. Officials stated that heavy dust clouds reduced visibility to zero, preventing the driver from seeing the soldiers at a forward post. Both victims were declared dead on arrival at the hospital.

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit ends without consensus on fossil fuels
articles.summary: The UN climate conference (COP31) in Turkiye failed to reach a consensus, marking the first such collapse since 2009. Developing nations, including India and China, expressed dissatisfaction over the dilution of historical responsibilities of developed countries. Disagreements persisted over the phase-out of fossil fuels and the lack of clarity on climate finance for developing nations.

articles.headline: Namma Metro ridership hits 31cr as revenue grows
articles.summary: Bengaluru’s Namma Metro recorded 31 crore passenger boardings in 2025-26, a 12.3% increase from the previous year. While total revenue rose to Rs 1,624.6 crore due to higher ridership and fare revisions, overall losses widened to Rs 1,717.4 crore because of high finance costs. The launch of the Yellow Line significantly contributed to the increased passenger traffic.

articles.headline: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri and four others
articles.summary: The FSSAI has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International and four other firms after food safety tests flagged packaged water, chilli powder, and turmeric as unsafe or substandard. Violations included the presence of pesticide residues, excess bromate, and non-permitted colors. The regulator also suspended the licenses of two other establishments over hygiene concerns.

articles.headline: Bengal BJP MLA Rekha Patra hospitalized with poisoning symptoms
articles.summary: Rekha Patra, the BJP MLA from Hingalganj who led the Sandeshkhali movement, is on ventilator support in a Kolkata hospital. She was admitted with symptoms of poisoning, though officials are still awaiting final reports to confirm the cause. Family members reportedly mentioned the ingestion of an agricultural pesticide. Patra had recently expressed resentment against local party leaders.

articles.headline: US House Democrats secure historic majority in general election
articles.summary: House Democrats have won at least 258 seats, their best general election result since 1992. The sweep creates a divided government with Republicans controlling the White House while Democrats lead the House. The milestone follows intense voter focus on the cost of living and the Iran war. Emboldened Democrats plan a 100-day agenda to address economic issues and executive oversight.

articles.headline: Karnataka to increase minimum housing site size to 30x40ft
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has decided to increase the minimum size of residential sites allotted under government housing schemes from 20x30 feet to 30x40 feet. CM DK Shivakumar directed the revenue department to amend provisions to ensure families can build decent homes. The initiative aims to provide 15 lakh sites across the state, with the first 5 lakh to be allotted by January 2027.

articles.headline: Unaccompanied Indian children in US custody see sharp decline
articles.summary: US Border Protection data shows the number of unaccompanied Indian children in custody dropped from 730 in FY23 to 51 in FY26. Experts attribute the decline to tougher enforcement and quicker deportations, which have discouraged the tactic of using minors to facilitate family immigration. Overall, US authorities recorded 30,528 encounters with Indian nationals in FY26.

articles.headline: Cops summon writer Ravi Hanj over Basavanna book controversy
articles.summary: Belagavi police have summoned US-based writer Ravi Hanj for questioning on November 26 regarding his book on social reformer Basavanna. The move follows a complaint alleging that the book contains derogatory remarks against the Lingayat icon. The Karnataka government had previously ordered the confiscation of the book's copies following protests from the Lingayat community.

articles.headline: Navy relaxes rules to allow Agniveers to marry
articles.summary: The Indian Navy has updated its policy to allow Agniveers who opt for a two-year extension after their initial four-year service to get married. This relaxation comes as the first batch of recruits completes its first term. The 'Second Tour of Duty' also includes increased monthly pay and higher government contributions to the Seva Nidhi fund to make the extension more attractive.

articles.headline: Court orders compensation for blade found in soap
articles.summary: A Gwalior consumer court ordered Dettol’s manufacturer and retailers to pay Rs 54,000 to a family after a blade was found inside a soap bar. The complaint was filed after a minor boy suffered a cut on his cheek while bathing. The commission ruled that the company failed to prove adequate quality checks, finding them guilty of service deficiency and unfair trade practices.

articles.headline: BMTC audit uncovers Rs 4 crore inventory fraud
articles.summary: An internal audit of the BMTC Central Store-1 has revealed irregularities exceeding Rs 4 crore involving forged bills and missing spare parts. The fraud spanned five financial years and involved falsifying computer records to hide shortages of thousands of components. Wilson Garden police registered an FIR naming 21 accused, including serving and retired officials and a private supplier.

articles.headline: YS Sharmila stopped by police near family bungalow
articles.summary: High drama occurred on Bagalur Main Road as police intercepted APCC president YS Sharmila and her mother while they were heading towards a family bungalow. The property is currently occupied by her brother, YS Jagan Mohan Reddy. Citing a court order and potential law and order issues, police diverted Sharmila's vehicle to an alternative route to her hotel.

articles.headline: ED flags large-scale malpractices in 13 KPSC recruitments
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has detailed widespread irregularities in 13 KPSC recruitment notifications, including OMR sheet tampering and cash-for-jobs deals. Evidence suggests illegal gratifications ranged from Rs 40 lakh to Rs 1 crore per candidate. The agency has sought further action from the SIT, citing missing CCTV footage and irregular selection committee meetings.

articles.headline: Quick-commerce app Blinkit fined for delivering expired chocolates
articles.summary: A consumer commission fined Blinkit Rs 43,000 for delivering a gift box containing expired chocolates on Valentine's Day. A customer found three of the six items in the box were months past their expiry date. The court found the company guilty of unfair trade practices and ordered punitive damages, emphasizing that the seller cannot exploit consumer trust by stocking expired food.

articles.headline: Police launch massive crackdown on rowdy-sheeters in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Bengaluru police conducted surprise early-morning raids on the residences of rowdy-sheeters and habitual offenders across the city. The operation involved verifying current addresses, workplaces, and associates of known criminals to prevent unlawful activities. In the North division alone, 374 vehicles were checked and liquor was seized from one residence. Cops issued strict warnings to all.

articles.headline: Kaiga nuclear plant Unit-1 attains criticality after refurbishment
articles.summary: Kaiga Generating Station Unit-1 in Karnataka reached criticality for the second time following extensive life-extension and refurbishment work. The 220MW unit was taken offline after 25 years of operation. Attaining criticality marks the start of a self-sustaining nuclear fission chain reaction, allowing the unit to resume power supply to the grid after final technical checks.

articles.headline: Bangladesh seeks renewal of 1996 Ganga Water Treaty
articles.summary: Bangladesh has shifted its stance, requesting India to initiate formal negotiations for the renewal of the 1996 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty before it expires in December. Previously seeking a new agreement, Dhaka now emphasizes fair sharing of water during the dry season. The Joint Rivers Commission met to finalize the annual report on the treaty's implementation and discuss future terms.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi clarifies Gaza remarks after ally criticism
articles.summary: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi clarified his stance on Israel and Gaza following criticism from allies like the CPM. He reportedly conveyed that while India maintains defense relations with Israel, its foreign policy cannot be dictated by Israeli interests. He condemned Israeli actions in Gaza as wrong while reiterating that the October 7 Hamas attacks were 'absolutely horrible'.

articles.headline: BIS hallmark helps identify rape-murder victim in Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: Railway police identified a 52-year-old woman raped and murdered in a train coach by tracing a BIS hallmark on her gold ring. The code 'TEAIL5' was traced to a hallmark center in Rajkot and eventually to a jeweler in Chhattisgarh. The victim, who was from Madhya Pradesh, had been missing since October 13. The suspect has been arrested and remanded in judicial custody.

articles.headline: NSEL victims to receive Rs 1,950 crore settlement today
articles.summary: Over 5,000 victims of the National Spot Exchange Ltd (NSEL) scam will receive Rs 1,950 crore in a one-time settlement. The funds were released by the Maharashtra government from assets attached and liquidated during the probe. The payout will be monitored by a court-appointed authority. The scam, which broke in 2013, involved siphoning investor funds through commodity trading.

articles.headline: IITian's startup sues Apple for Rs 1,500 crore over NameDrop
articles.summary: GG Technologies, founded by an IIT Delhi alumnus, has sued Apple in the Bombay High Court for alleged patent infringement regarding the 'NameDrop' contact-sharing feature. The startup claims Apple's feature mirrors its 'StayTouch' app technology patented in 2024. The firm is seeking Rs 1,500 crore in damages and an injunction against infringing Apple products.

articles.headline: Tata Steel approves sale of pipe business for Rs 28,000cr
articles.summary: The Tata Steel board has approved the sale of its steel tubes and pipes business and its 100% stake in Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo Tubes. The transactions are valued at approximately Rs 28,000 crore combined. The move is part of the company's strategy to divest non-core downstream assets. The deal is subject to regulatory approvals and will involve facilities in multiple states.

articles.headline: Chinese intelligence ran campaign to acquire AI chips, says report
articles.summary: A New York Times report claims China's Ministry of State Security has prioritized acquiring advanced semiconductor chips to overcome Western export curbs. The campaign involves helping Chinese firms smuggle chips and gathering global industry intelligence. This follows US investigations into alleged espionage attempts targeting Nvidia and efforts to secure computing power for Chinese military use.

articles.headline: 90% of elite Indian AI researchers work abroad, study finds
articles.summary: A study by the Carnegie Endowment reveals that 90% of India's elite AI researchers have left the country to work abroad, primarily in the US. While China produces 60% of top researchers and increasingly retains them, India struggles with talent production and retention. Not a single Indian institution featured among the top universities producing elite AI talent for the 2026 cohort.

articles.headline: NMC proposes easing medical licensing rules for foreign graduates
articles.summary: The National Medical Commission has proposed draft amendments to ease licensing requirements for Foreign Medical Graduates (FMGs). The changes seek to remove the mandate that graduates must hold a license in the country where they studied. Instead, FMGs would only need to be registered with the respective professional regulatory body, simplifying the process for practicing in India.

articles.headline: High resignation rates for PG doctors at govt hospitals flagged
articles.summary: RTI data revealed high resignation rates among post-graduate doctors at premier institutions like AIIMS and JIPMER. AIIMS Raipur saw 54 resignations in 2025, while JIPMER recorded 44. Doctors' bodies cited long working hours, lack of security, and low pay as reasons for the exodus to private hospitals. Public health advocates are calling for auditable duty-hour records and better facilities.

articles.headline: India considers $2-billion funding package for Nepal
articles.summary: India is evaluating a $2-billion grant and loan proposal from Nepal to support infrastructure, energy, and connectivity projects. The package was discussed during Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah's visit. Key focus areas include hydropower, railways, and cross-border infrastructure, aiming to counter regional competition while addressing Nepal's requests for additional air routes.

articles.headline: India mulls curbs on non-Basmati rice exports to rein domestic prices
articles.summary: The government is considering a ban or a minimum export price on non-Basmati white rice to control domestic food inflation, which hit 12.51% in October. While parboiled and Basmati rice may be excluded, the move aims to stabilize prices that have risen despite earlier measures. Total non-Basmati white rice exports reached 4.87 million tonnes by October this fiscal year.

articles.headline: Indian companies on global buying spree as M&A activity hits high
articles.summary: StanChart CEO PD Singh reports a significant surge in cross-border M&A activity as Indian firms seek global market access and intellectual property. Acquisitions are spanning sectors like automotive, chemicals, and manufacturing. The shift follows global supply chain realignments, with at least two multinational regional headquarters relocating to Karnataka every week.

articles.headline: VinFast eyes major four-wheeler expansion, slams brakes on e-bus plans
articles.summary: Vietnamese EV maker VinFast plans to scale up its upcoming Tamil Nadu plant capacity from 50,000 to 1.5 lakh four-wheelers annually. However, the company has paused its electric bus plans for India to focus on passenger cars and two-wheelers. The firm has already identified 34 cities for its dealership network and aims to localize 15% of its production components initially.

articles.headline: Indian Bank MD targets ₹35-lakh-crore business by 2032
articles.summary: Indian Bank MD and CEO Binod Kumar announced a long-term goal to reach a total business of ₹35-lakh-crore by 2032. The state-owned lender is focusing on digital transformation, including AI-driven credit models, and expanding its reach in RAM (retail, agriculture, and MSME) sectors to compete with private banks and improve its CASA ratio.

articles.headline: Start-ups bet on physical AI to transform factories and warehouses
articles.summary: Indian startups are developing 'physical AI' models that integrate sensors and machine learning into industrial robots. Unlike standard chatbots, these models allow robots to navigate complex real-world environments like factories and warehouses. Companies like Addverb and Innefu are leading this shift, with applications spanning logistics, security, and large-scale manufacturing.

articles.headline: CCPA slaps ₹10 lakh fine on anti-drone gun seller
articles.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority fined a company for selling anti-drone guns without mandatory regulatory clearances. The order emphasized that hosting or advertising such restricted electronic warfare equipment violates consumer rights and safety standards under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. The seller must also cease all advertisements for the product.

articles.headline: IPO Street set for year-end revival; 29 firms to raise ₹42,000 crore
articles.summary: Following a post-Diwali lull, India's primary market is set for a major revival with 29 companies planning to raise ₹42,000 crore through IPOs. Key upcoming listings include Carlsberg India (₹6,650 crore) and Avaada Electro (₹6,000 crore). Currently, 252 firms have filed for IPOs totaling ₹4.5 lakh crore, supported by resilient domestic investor interest and AI-driven growth stories.

articles.headline: SEBI working on scheme to train independent directors
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India is developing a capacity-building network to train independent directors. Partnering with institutions like the ICAI and IIMs, the initiative aims to enhance board-level oversight and equip directors with skills to navigate the evolving startup and entrepreneurial ecosystem. The scheme will focus on technical expertise and ethical governance.

articles.headline: How the Singhanias are tuning legacy land for modern real estate
articles.summary: The Singhania family of the JK Group is pivoting its legacy textile and industrial land parcels toward premium residential and mixed-use real estate projects. Through JK UrbanScapes, the group is developing luxury housing in Kanpur and exploring projects in Banaras and Haryana. The portfolio includes 90-acre developments and historical industrial sites being repurposed for modern use.

articles.headline: Power Ministers' meet to focus on resource adequacy and smart meters
articles.summary: State Power Ministers are scheduled to meet in New Delhi on November 27 to discuss power sector reforms. Key agenda items include ensuring resource adequacy, the financial viability of distribution companies (discoms), and the implementation of smart metering. The meet will also address renewable energy integration and the development of power evacuation infrastructure.

articles.headline: Ashok Leyland expands EV push, eyes light commercial vehicle market
articles.summary: Ashok Leyland's electric arm, Switch Mobility, is targeting the light commercial vehicle (LCV) segment for growth. The company plans to deploy over 200 e-trucks for distribution and is investing ₹324 crore in Switch Mobility UK. Production is slated to begin in 2027, with the firm aiming for 48% and 56% market share in various electric truck and bus categories by FY27.

articles.headline: Telangana delegation in Paris to woo investments in electronics and aviation
articles.summary: A high-level Telangana delegation, led by Deputy CM Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, is visiting France to attract investments. The team met with Schneider Electric and Safran Aircraft Engines to discuss expansion plans in the state. Telangana aims to leverage its existing aerospace and electronics ecosystem to secure new manufacturing and M&A projects from global firms.

articles.headline: India-EU trade pact likely to be signed on December 27
articles.summary: India and the 27-nation European Union are expected to sign a free trade agreement (FTA) on December 27 in New Delhi. The deal aims to boost bilateral trade and investment, following a visit by French President Emmanuel Macron. The FTA is seen as a significant step in strengthening India's economic ties with Europe and diversifying its global trade partnerships.

articles.headline: Engineering goods exports rise 36% in Oct on strong US shipments
articles.summary: India's engineering exports grew by 36% year-on-year to $12.74 billion in October 2025, driven by strong demand from the US and UK. High shipments of iron and steel, copper, and electrical machinery contributed to the growth. However, exports to Saudi Arabia and Vietnam saw a decline. The US remains the top destination, with cumulative exports reaching $14.4 billion this fiscal year.

articles.headline: CII proposes 15 priority reforms for the financial sector
articles.summary: The Confederation of Indian Industry has proposed 15 reforms to modernize India's financial sector and support growth. Recommendations include a calibrated priority sector lending framework, reforms in bankruptcy laws for NBFCs, and a focus on climate risk. The CII estimates that India will need $106 trillion in financial assets by 2047 to support its goal of becoming a $26.5 trillion economy.

articles.headline: Panel to review proposals aimed at GST relief for businesses
articles.summary: A GST Council standing committee is reviewing five key changes to protect bone fide input tax credit (ITC) recipients from fraud. Proposals include allowing ITC when a supplier has failed to pay tax, provided the recipient was not involved in the fraud. The move aims to simplify compliance and prevent genuine businesses from being penalized for the defaults of others in the supply chain.

articles.headline: Pilots’ body seeks financial review of SpiceJet over safety concerns
articles.summary: The Federation of Indian Pilots has requested the DGCA to conduct a financial and safety audit of SpiceJet. The pilots cited concerns over delayed salaries, unpaid dues, and the airline's overall financial stress, which they believe could impact operational safety. The DGCA has already issued a show cause notice to the airline regarding flight cancellations and operational issues.

articles.headline: Anthropic's Nasdaq listing: A giant move for AI and technology
articles.summary: Anthropic's IPO, valuing the company at $1.5 trillion, is a landmark moment for the AI industry. The listing highlights the massive investment in AI and the potential for these technologies to transform global business. However, concerns remain about safety and the need for safeguards to prevent AI from outpacing human control and ethical standards.

articles.headline: Sailing between Scylla and Charybdis: Navigating India's economic policy
articles.summary: India's economic policy faces the dual challenge of controlling inflation while supporting growth. Historical parallels with the 1970s and 80s highlight the difficulty of managing high food and energy prices. The government must balance fiscal discipline with the need for investment in infrastructure and technology to ensure long-term stability and prosperity.

articles.headline: COP's electricity goals are ambitious but require massive investment
articles.summary: The COP31 goal to shift 35% of energy demand to electricity by 2035 is ambitious but faces significant hurdles. India will need to invest heavily in renewable energy, storage, and transmission infrastructure. The transition from fossil fuels to clean energy requires global cooperation and financial support for developing nations to achieve these ambitious targets.

articles.headline: Defining Genocide at the International Court of Justice
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice is grappling with the definition of genocide in various global conflicts. A recent ruling regarding allegations of 'genocide' against Israel has brought the issue to the forefront. The case highlights the complexities of international law and the challenges of hold nations accountable for human rights violations in a divided global landscape.

articles.headline: Who is liable for UPI frauds? A look at consumer protection
articles.summary: A recent court ruling has sparked debate over liability in UPI-related frauds. While consumers are often held responsible for sharing details, the role of banks and third-party app providers (TPAPs) is being scrutinized. Current laws may not fully protect consumers from sophisticated phishing and technical breaches, highlighting the need for updated regulations in the digital payment era.

articles.headline: Kitchenware makers caught between rising costs and price-sensitive consumers
articles.summary: Indian kitchenware manufacturers are facing a squeeze on margins due to rising raw material costs, particularly aluminum and stainless steel. While prices have risen by 50%, firms are unable to fully pass these costs to consumers. Companies like TTK Prestige and Stovekraft are shifting to more cost-effective materials and triple-ply products to maintain sales in a competitive market.

articles.headline: COP31 President criticized for 'best COP ever' comment
articles.summary: The President of COP31, Murat Kurum, has faced criticism from civil society groups for calling the summit the 'best COP ever' despite limited progress on climate finance and fossil fuel transition. Environmentalists and some nations expressed disappointment over the lack of concrete commitments and the slow pace of negotiations, highlighting the deep divide between global climate goals and action.

articles.headline: Share the solar panel, split the power bill through virtual metering
articles.summary: Virtual net metering (VNM) is being touted as a way to boost solar adoption in urban India. VNM allows multiple consumers to share a solar plant on a common roof and split the power bill. While the concept has potential, high installation costs and complex application processes remain hurdles. Reforms and standardized billing are needed to make VNM a viable option for residential and commercial areas.

articles.headline: Personal guarantees haunt promoters as lenders turn on the heat
articles.summary: Indian promoters are increasingly facing the consequences of personal guarantees signed for corporate loans. With stricter rules, lenders are pursuing personal assets of high-profile names like the Dhoots of Videocon and Anil Ambani. This shift aims to ensure promoter accountability and recover dues from insolvent firms, marking a significant change in India's corporate bankruptcy landscape.

articles.headline: For Delhi Metro, the next stop is the global rail market
articles.summary: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) is eyeing the global market for its operations and maintenance expertise. Its subsidiary, DMIL, is pitching for mass rapid transit projects in the Philippines, Sri Lanka, and West Asian countries. With experience in managing a 400-km network, DMRC aims to become a global leader in urban rail solutions and secure lucrative international contracts.

articles.headline: Space labs tethered to floating balloons: A new frontier for research
articles.summary: Red Balloon Aerospace is developing high-altitude balloon platforms to conduct space-like research at a fraction of the cost of rocket launches. These tethered balloons can carry scientific instruments and communications equipment to the stratosphere. The startup aims to provide a sustainable and affordable platform for testing space technology and atmospheric monitoring.

articles.headline: PM tells DRDO to deepen R&D partnership with private firms
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) to open up its R&D and labs to private companies. The move aims to boost India's domestic defense manufacturing and reduce dependence on imports. DRDO is expected to share its research and technology to foster innovation and help Indian firms compete in the global defense market.

articles.headline: UN climate talks fail over shift away from fossil fuels
articles.summary: The latest UN climate talks have ended in an impasse as nations failed to reach a consensus on shifting away from fossil fuels. Developed nations and environmental groups have expressed disappointment over the lack of a clear commitment to end the use of oil, gas, and coal. The deadlock highlights the ongoing challenges in achieving global cooperation for climate action.

articles.headline: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against companies over unsafe food samples
articles.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has sanctioned prosecution against several companies for selling unsafe food products. Samples of walnut kernels, fennel, and other items were found to be non-compliant with safety standards, including high levels of pesticides and contaminants. The move is part of a wider effort to ensure food safety and protect public health.

articles.headline: Kerala seizes unsafe cosmetics after girl develops kidney disease
articles.summary: The Kerala government launched 'Operation Soundarya' to seize illegal cosmetic products following reports of a 17-year-old girl developing kidney disease from a mercury-laced fairness cream. Inspections led to the seizure of fake products worth over ₹10 lakh. Authorities found the cream contained 12,500 ppm of mercury, far exceeding the permitted limit of 1 ppm.

articles.headline: Karnataka issues notification to forfeit controversial Basava Mantapa book
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has authorized the forfeiture of NRI author Ravi Hanj’s book 'Basava Mantapa' in both print and digital formats. The notification follows a Cabinet decision to preserve public order after protests alleged the book contained defamatory content regarding social reformer Basavanna. The author was recently detained at Kochi airport while attempting to leave India.

articles.headline: Voters challenge names deleted from final electoral rolls in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Numerous residents in Bengaluru have filed over 350 appeals after their names were excluded from the final electoral rolls despite participating in the Special Intensive Revision process. Citizens expressed frustration over inconsistent outcomes and technical discrepancies. Some officials have reportedly advised excluded voters to apply afresh, which may bar them from upcoming local elections.

articles.headline: India and France mark 60 years of space partnership
articles.summary: India and France are strengthening their decades-old space ties with the joint TRISHNA mission for thermal infrared earth observation. The partnership between ISRO and CNES focuses on climate change and water resource management. Both nations emphasized 'strategic autonomy' and are exploring increased industry-level collaboration and manufacturing within the Indian space ecosystem.

articles.headline: Likud and Yashar resume coalition government talks in Israel
articles.summary: Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party and Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party have resumed negotiations to form a broad coalition government. Following inconclusive October elections, Likud is pushing for policies that exclude Arab parties. Eisenkot has until December 6 to finalize a government, with a possible 14-day extension as the bloc remains divided over partners.

articles.headline: New Traffic Commissioner prioritizes management over enforcement in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Hemant M. Nimbalkar, Bengaluru's new Traffic Commissioner, stated that his priority is reducing congestion rather than aggressive penalty enforcement. He announced that officers should not stop vehicles unless a visible safety violation occurs. Plans include deploying senior officials at junctions during peak hours and using AI and big data to solve the city's notorious traffic issues.

articles.headline: Helmetless riding violations in Bengaluru double to 42.9 lakh
articles.summary: Traffic police data reveals that 42.9 lakh challans were issued for riding without a helmet in Bengaluru during the first 10 months of 2026, more than double the total for 2025. Contactless enforcement through cameras now accounts for over 92% of cases. Senior officials are calling for higher penalties to deter the rampant violation and improve commuter behavior.

articles.headline: Sitharaman highlights systemic shift in India's poverty reduction strategy
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that government policies over the last decade have moved from temporary cash transfers to removing systemic barriers to poverty. She noted that extreme poverty dropped to 2.6% in 2023. Key initiatives like Jan Dhan accounts, Ayushman Bharat, and the Jal Jeevan Mission were cited as critical tools for long-term financial and health protection.

articles.headline: Manipur hooch tragedy death toll rises to 17
articles.summary: The death toll from consuming spurious liquor in Manipur has reached 17, with 228 people still hospitalized. Samples of the local country liquor have been sent to Kolkata for testing. The state government has launched a high-level inquiry and arrested six individuals. Raids across the state have resulted in the seizure of 4,600 liters of illicit alcohol.

articles.headline: U.S. probes Nvidia’s accounting practices amid AI chip scrutiny
articles.summary: U.S. officials are investigating Nvidia’s financial disclosures and accounting practices following the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang. The inquiry reportedly focuses on the company’s reporting of sales by geographical location and its dealings with Megaspeed, a firm suspected of shipping restricted AI chips to China. The probe is currently in its early stages.

articles.headline: Global stock sell-off erases $9 trillion in market value
articles.summary: World stock markets have seen nearly $9 trillion wiped off their value since August, with Taiwan experiencing a sharp 17% plunge. The sell-off intensified due to expectations that major economies, including the U.S., will require further interest rate hikes to combat persistent inflation. The market downturn marks one of the most significant declines since the early 1990s.

articles.headline: Grand Theft Auto VI breaks records with $3.79 billion launch
articles.summary: Rockstar Games announced that Grand Theft Auto VI has set a new record for entertainment launches, grossing $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales. The game sold 32.5 million units prior to its official release across all platforms. The launch marks the biggest financial debut in the history of the entertainment industry.

articles.headline: Labour Ministry launches NCS ONE job-matching portal and skill gap index
articles.summary: The Union Ministry of Labour and Employment launched the National Career Service (NCS) Open Network for Employment (ONE) Portal to connect jobseekers with private and state platforms. Union Minister Mansukh Mandaviya also introduced the Occupational Shortage Index to identify labour market gaps and an e-Shram Livelihood Profile Module to track social security for unorganised workers.

articles.headline: Listed IT majors struggle to match India's booming software services exports
articles.summary: Revenue growth of India's 10 largest listed IT firms has failed to keep pace with national software exports. Combined net sales of these firms fell to a 20-year low of 45.8% of total exports in FY26, down from a 71.9% peak in FY18. While national software exports rose 12.8% to $203.7 billion in FY26, the top 10 firms grew just 3.6%, partly due to the rise of global capability centres.

articles.headline: Centre proposes sharing fertiliser subsidy costs with state governments
articles.summary: The government is considering a model to share the urea subsidy burden with states using a pre-fixed formula to improve oversight and curb non-farm diversion. The proposal involves turning urea subsidy from a Central Sector Scheme into a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, potentially requiring states to share costs in ratios like 60:40 or 50:50, similar to the VB-GRAM G rural employment model.

articles.headline: Indian armed forces turn to startups for next-gen combat technology
articles.summary: India's military is increasingly collaborating with domestic startups to develop autonomous underwater vehicles, firefighting robots, and AI-driven vision systems. Officials at the Bengaluru Tech Summit emphasized co-development and funding to address manufacturing gaps. India spent $92.1 billion on its military in 2025, the world's fifth-largest expenditure, seeking indigenous solutions.

articles.headline: Hospitals divided over impact of government cap on cancer drug margins
articles.summary: Leading hospital chains like Fortis and Apollo are assessing the impact of a 30% trade margin cap on 137 oncology drugs that took effect in November. While Fortis expects potential pressure on profitability, Manipal and Aster DM Healthcare see limited impact as chemotherapy is only a small portion of revenue. The industry is advocating for a shift toward service-based pricing frameworks.

articles.headline: Drug firms flag concerns over NPPA's frequent use of emergency powers
articles.summary: Pharmaceutical companies have raised concerns that the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) is increasingly using Paragraph 19 'emergency' powers to fix prices. The clause has been invoked five times in 2026 for measures like trade margin caps on cancer drugs. Industry executives warn that repeated interventions reduce regulatory predictability and may impact future investments.

articles.headline: Pilot federation urges MoCA to restrict SpiceJet operations over finances
articles.summary: The Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) has asked the Ministry of Civil Aviation to direct the DGCA to restrict SpiceJet’s operating capacity. The body cited concerns that delayed salaries and financial stress could impact safety. FIP also called for verification of the airline's proposed ~5,500 crore fundraising and an assessment of its maintenance capabilities and crew strength.

articles.headline: Adani successfully tests 8-km vehicle-mounted anti-tank guided missile
articles.summary: Adani Defence and Aerospace test-fired the Bagheera AT1 anti-tank guided missile at Pokhran. The laser beam-riding missile has an engagement range of 8 km, double that of the Army's Nag missile, and successfully hit targets at 10 km during trials. The system is designed for a 4x4 armoured vehicle with an automated launcher, aiming to reduce vulnerability to radio-frequency jamming.

articles.headline: Reliance Brands FY26 revenue grows 3.8% to ~3,390.9 crore
articles.summary: Reliance Brands Limited (RBL), a subsidiary of Reliance Retail, reported a 3.77 per cent increase in FY26 revenue to ~3,390.89 crore. According to RoC filings, the company narrowed its loss to ~137.04 crore from a profit of ~237.12 crore in the previous fiscal year. RBL operates several global fashion partnerships and retail operations in the Indian market.

articles.headline: Shree Cement targets 100 million tonne capacity within four years
articles.summary: Shree Cement, India’s third-largest cement maker, expects to surpass 100 million tonnes per annum production capacity in the next three to four years. Chairman Hari Mohan Bangur stated the firm is targeting a CAGR of 9-10 per cent, driven by infrastructure and housing demand. The aggressive expansion push aims for growth higher than the industry average of 7-8 per cent.

articles.headline: Chalet Hotels plans ~3,500 crore expansion over next three years
articles.summary: Chalet Hotels is set to invest approximately ~3,500 crore over three years to expand its hospitality portfolio. MD and CEO Shwetank Singh noted that the upcoming Taj-branded hotel at Delhi International Airport will now open nearly 200 rooms in Q1FY28. The expansion includes a 380-room Taj property, though completion faced slight delays due to pollution-linked construction restrictions.

articles.headline: Vietnam's VinFast to enter Indian electric two-wheeler market in 2027
articles.summary: Vietnam-based auto giant VinFast plans to enter India's electric two-wheeler market in 2027, with manufacturing based at its Thoothukudi facility in Tamil Nadu. The company also aims to introduce two electric compact SUVs annually starting in early 2025. VinFast targets a 50,000-unit annual capacity at its Indian plant and plans to increase local sourcing to 30 per cent.

articles.headline: Google pledges $5 million to IIT Kharagpur for AI research
articles.summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai has facilitated a $5 million pledge to his alma mater, IIT Kharagpur, to advance AI research and expand educational opportunities. Announced during the institute's platinum jubilee, the funding aims to develop the next generation of technology professionals and strengthen advanced artificial intelligence research initiatives at the campus.

articles.headline: TDB shortlists 11 startups for second Research and Innovation funding cohort
articles.summary: The Technology Development Board (TDB) has shortlisted its second cohort of 11 startups, including Perceptyne, SigTuple, and CynLr, for funding under the government's ~1 trillion RDI fund. The new cohort focuses on application-oriented technologies like industrial robotics and AI healthcare. TDB's total sanctioned allocation has reached ~3,000 crore from an initial ~2,000 crore.

articles.headline: OrbitAID to conduct India's first on-orbit satellite refuelling demo
articles.summary: Chennai-based startup OrbitAID plans to conduct India's first commercial satellite refuelling mission by late 2027. A precursor demonstration mission is scheduled for next month in Low Earth Orbit using a mini tanker satellite. The company, which recently raised $2.5 million, aims to provide 'satellite-as-a-service' including debris management and life-extension for existing satellites.

articles.headline: Economists project 7.7% Q2 GDP growth despite El Nino impacts
articles.summary: Median forecasts from 11 agencies peg India's Q2FY27 GDP growth at 7.7 per cent, slightly below the 7.8 per cent seen in Q1. High-frequency indicators show resilient manufacturing and bank credit growth, though government capital expenditure slowed. Sub-par monsoons are expected to have weighed on agricultural growth, which may fall below 1 per cent for the quarter.

articles.headline: CII proposes permanent liquidity window for NBFCs and PSL revamp
articles.summary: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) has submitted 15 recommendations to a high-level banking committee, including a rule-based liquidity and refinance window for NBFCs. CII also proposed raising the voting rights cap in private banks to 49 per cent and allowing pension funds to invest in corporate bonds rated below AA to meet India's long-term financing needs.

articles.headline: India's cyber insurance market projected to treble by FY31
articles.summary: A report by Deloitte estimates India’s cyber insurance market will grow from $115-255 million in FY25 to $321-594 million by FY31. The growth is driven by rising cyber incidents, cloud adoption, and DPDP Act compliance. Large tech and IT firms are leading the demand, with some banking policyholders doubling their coverage limits to $50-100 million recently.

articles.headline: CBIC proposes GST amendments to protect genuine buyers from ITC loss
articles.summary: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) has drafted a proposal to amend the GST law, ensuring genuine buyers do not lose Input Tax Credit (ITC) solely due to a supplier's invalid claims. A new Section 16A would deny credit only if investigation proves the recipient knowingly assisted in fraudulent invoicing. The move aims to curb fake invoicing while shielding honest taxpayers.

articles.headline: Battery energy storage market moves from tendering to execution phase
articles.summary: Ratings agency Icra reports that India's battery energy storage system (BESS) market is transitioning to execution, supported by strong policy and a large tender pipeline. Rapid renewable capacity addition is causing grid congestion in Rajasthan and Gujarat, making storage critical. However, rising battery prices and rupee depreciation remain key challenges for project viability.

articles.headline: ESIC notifies new scheme rules to automate sickness and maternity benefits
articles.summary: The Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) has notified the 2026 General Regulations, allowing automatic processing of sickness and maternity benefits through direct benefit transfer. The rules replace 1950 regulations and align with the Code on Social Security 2020. Eligible claims will no longer require separate applications if Aadhaar-linked bank and medical data are available.

articles.headline: West Bengal govt in talks to acquire 997 acres in Singur
articles.summary: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari stated the West Bengal government is negotiating with farmers to acquire 997 acres of land in Singur, the former site of Tata Motors' Nano project. This follows an announcement by Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar that Ashok Leyland plans to set up a truck manufacturing plant at the site. The land was originally returned to farmers after a 2016 Supreme Court order.

articles.headline: IndusInd Bank invokes clawback provisions against former CEO Sumant Kathpalia
articles.summary: IndusInd Bank's board has decided to invoke malus and clawback provisions against former MD & CEO Sumant Kathpalia, effective retrospectively from March 2020. The bank also terminated his employment following an enquiry report regarding accounting discrepancies in its derivatives portfolio. Kathpalia had resigned in April 2025, taking responsibility for the issues.

articles.headline: India and Nepal set broad development and energy agenda for PM talks
articles.summary: Nepalese PM Balendra Shah arrived in New Delhi for his first bilateral visit, where he will meet PM Narendra Modi to discuss a possible $2 billion development package. Key agenda items include hydropower trade, rail connectivity, and climate resilience. The package would fund reconstruction after Nepal's August floods. A 10-year power agreement targeting 10,000 MW exports is also in focus.

articles.headline: Indian Army reportedly buying Chinese drone parts despite official ban
