articles.summary: Smit Shah, president of the Drone Federation of India, alleged that Indian Army units are specifically requesting Chinese drone components for training and sensitisation, bypassing official bans. While large tenders reject Chinese parts, smaller local procurements reportedly still feature them. The federation has written to the Chief of Defence Staff seeking a blanket ban on Chinese-origin parts.

articles.headline: Uncertainty looms over Winter Session of Parliament amid delimitation speculation
articles.summary: Uncertainty persists over Parliament’s Winter Session dates as the Monsoon Session remains unprorogued for a record 101 days. Speculation suggests the government may call a special session to pass constitutional amendments for women’s reservation and delimitation. Proposed changes could increase Lok Sabha seats to 850, though Opposition parties demand a freeze at the current 543 seats.

articles.headline: Attacks on Awami League activists in Bangladesh leave 30 houses burned
articles.summary: Political violence spread in Bangladesh’s Narail district as supporters of the ruling BNP allegedly set fire to nearly 30 houses belonging to Awami League leaders. Properties targeted included the residence of a former lawmaker. Security forces have deployed 95 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh across several districts to maintain order following the killings of two BNP leaders last week.

articles.headline: Anthropic's record Nasdaq debut fails to calm AI spending fears
articles.summary: AI startup Anthropic touched a $2 trillion valuation on its first day of trading before shares fell 9 per cent. Despite raising $120 billion in investor funds, the debut highlighted Wall Street doubts regarding the financial viability of massive AI infrastructure spending. Stocks of other AI bellwethers like Nvidia and AMD also fell by double digits as investors reassessed the tech cycle.

articles.headline: Latest COP31 draft pact omits mention of fossil fuel phase-out
articles.summary: A new draft climate agreement at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, does not contain the words 'fossil fuels' or call for a transition away from coal, oil, and gas. The proposal, which focuses on carbon capture technology and electrification, has been rejected by the EU and other nations. Negotiators passed the original deadline as several countries vowed to block a deal that ignores the drivers of warming.

articles.headline: Editorial: PM Modi rebukes India Inc over jobs and self-reliance
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in a speech at Ficci, criticized industry captains for failing to do enough on job creation and wage increases. He urged India Inc to move beyond short-term growth and government protections like tariff barriers and tax cuts. The PM called for self-reflection and investment in building global competitiveness to lower import dependence and achieve long-term goals.

articles.headline: Weddings and festivals expected to boost paint sector Q3 revenue
articles.summary: The paints sector expects strong volume and revenue growth in Q3FY27, driven by a late festive season and wedding demand. Analysts note that aggregate revenue growth in Q2 reached 17% despite high competitive intensity. Easing raw material costs and price hikes since March are expected to improve margins, with market leaders like Asian Paints and Berger Paints seeing recent stock price rallies.

articles.headline: Deepinder Goyal's Temple wearable sparks medical and regulatory debate
articles.summary: Deepinder Goyal's new startup, Temple, has launched a ~85,000 wearable device claiming to monitor brain blood flow. While Goyal has invested $20 million of his own money, some doctors question the device's scientific efficacy and sample size of its studies. The venture also faces questions regarding its classification as a wellness device versus a medical device requiring CDSCO clearance.

articles.headline: Delhi's outdoor workers struggle as pollution triggers GRAP construction bans
articles.summary: Migrant construction and gig workers in Delhi face unemployment and severe health risks as air pollution triggers Stage III GRAP restrictions. Bans on non-essential construction leave thousands without daily wages or shelter at work sites. Gig workers report respiratory issues due to 11-hour road exposure, while unions report that workers have yet to receive compensation from welfare boards.

articles.headline: Mahindra Financial evaluates acquiring gold finance companies to boost credit
articles.summary: Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services is exploring acquisitions of gold loan companies like Indel Money, Kosamattam Finance, and ICL Fincorp. The move aims to diversify its revenue streams beyond vehicle financing into the fast-growing gold credit segment. The company currently has a loan book of over ₹8,000 crore in its target segment.

articles.headline: Pernod Ricard considers Indian IPO as market becomes second largest globally
articles.summary: French distiller Pernod Ricard may hold its January board meeting in India to discuss a local IPO. India has become the company's second-largest market after the US. A listing would require a 25% public float. The company's Indian revenue grew to ₹13,315 crore in FY26, driven by brands like Chivas Regal and Royal Stag.

articles.headline: Sensex surges 20 percent in dollar terms driven by foreign fund inflows
articles.summary: The Sensex has risen 20% in dollar terms this quarter, signaling a bull market. Gains were driven by rising share prices (15-16%) and rupee appreciation (4-5%). Foreign portfolio investors have pumped $14.33 billion into Indian markets since October 16. The Nifty 50 also gained 18.2% during this period.

articles.headline: Mastercard expands focus on India B2B payments market for SMEs and corporates
articles.summary: Mastercard is doubling down on India’s commercial payments sector, targeting SMEs and large corporations. The strategy focuses on overcoming B2B friction and improving reconciliation processes. The company is engaging with various banks to support the ecosystem, viewing India as a critical growth market with significant innovation potential.

articles.headline: Government considers import duty cuts on over 115 manufacturing intermediate goods
articles.summary: India is weighing a 1-3% cut in import duties for products including chemicals, auto parts, and polyester fibre to boost manufacturing competitiveness. The finance ministry is reviewing recommendations for the FY28 budget. The move aims to reduce production costs, as India's 6.8% average tariff on inputs currently trails competitors like China and Vietnam.

articles.headline: Oyo parent Oravel Stays plans Q4 IPO at 2.1 billion dollar valuation
articles.summary: Hospitality firm Oravel Stays (Oyo) is preparing for an IPO in the January-March quarter with a projected valuation of $2.1-2.3 billion. This is the company's third attempt at going public. Operating revenue grew 50% year-on-year to ₹9,358 crore in FY26, with net profit rising to ₹994 crore, aided by deferred tax credits.

articles.headline: India dominates New Zealand with record 720 runs in Basin Reserve Test
articles.summary: India declared at 720/9, their highest-ever away total and the highest by any team in New Zealand. Centuries from Rishabh Pant (128) and KL Rahul (136) anchored the innings. New Zealand ended the fourth day at 119/2, trailing by 232 runs. Pant's performance made him the second-highest six-hitter in Test history with 108 career sixes.

articles.headline: Barcelona stage dramatic comeback to beat Villarreal three-two in La Liga
articles.summary: Barcelona restored their three-point lead in La Liga with a 3-2 victory over Villarreal. Despite trailing by two goals early on, Hansi Flick's side scored three times in 11 minutes during the second half. Goals from Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez, plus a Pau Navarro own goal, secured the win. Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty.

articles.headline: India thrashes Thailand seven-nil to reach Women’s Asian Champions Trophy semifinals
articles.summary: Defending champions India secured a semifinal spot in the Women's Asian Champions Trophy with a 7-0 win over Thailand. Deepika scored a hat-trick, while Navneet Kaur added two goals. Mumtaz Khan and Sunelita Toppo also contributed to the scoreline. India and Japan have both advanced to the semifinals with two matches remaining.

articles.headline: Josh Hazlewood addresses Usman Khawaja's autobiography regarding ball-tampering scandal
articles.summary: Australian fast bowler Josh Hazlewood stated he bears no resentment toward Usman Khawaja over his new book "Sabr." The autobiography touches upon team dynamics during the 2018 ball-tampering scandal. Hazlewood acknowledged the team wasn't perfectly close at the time but maintained a professional relationship with his former teammate.

articles.headline: Tata Play negotiates sale of broadband business to ACT Fibernet
articles.summary: Tata Play is in talks to sell its broadband division to Atria Convergence Technologies (ACT). Tata Play seeks ₹1,500 crore for the 650,000-subscriber business, while ACT has offered ₹800 crore. The move follows a decline in traditional DTH revenues. ACT recently exited cable operations to focus on its fiber-to-the-home business.

articles.headline: Coca-Cola revives Gold Spot orange drink as low-sugar beverage option
articles.summary: Coca-Cola is set to relaunch Gold Spot, an orange carbonated drink phased out 26 years ago, as a low-sugar and no-sugar variant. The move targets the health-conscious market and aims to compete with rising local rivals like Reliance's Campa. The brand was originally acquired from Parle Bisleri in 1993.

articles.headline: Income Tax Department uncovers 2,700 crore rupee Chinese gaming payment network
articles.summary: Authorities busted an online gaming network controlled by Chinese entities that used Indian shell companies to collect ₹2,700 crore. The network used a platform called 1stPe to facilitate UPI payments. Investigations led to the seizure of $650,000 in cryptocurrency and the discovery of undisclosed luxury apartments in Dubai.

articles.headline: AI boom shifts to bond market as infrastructure costs rise
articles.summary: Franklin Templeton CEO Jenny Johnson states that artificial intelligence is evolving from an equity play into a significant bond market story. High infrastructure costs for data centers and chips are driving massive debt requirements. She anticipates US interest rates will remain chronic, potentially raising the bar for investments in emerging markets.

articles.headline: India and Belarus to expand partnership in agriculture, defence, and pharma
articles.summary: During a visit by Belarusian foreign minister Maxim Ryzhenkov, India and Belarus agreed to enhance industrial ties. Focus areas include assembling agricultural machinery in India and pharmaceutical production in Belarus. Discussions also covered the supply of potash and potential joint ventures in unmanned aerial vehicles.

articles.headline: Ladakh administration urges high voter turnout for upcoming council elections
articles.summary: Ladakh Chief Secretary Ashish Kundra has called for participation in the LAHDC elections scheduled for December 4. He stated that formal dialogue regarding constitutional safeguards under Article 371 will resume after the polls. Local groups continue to protest for statehood and land protections, though the government promises a representative body.

articles.headline: UAE seeks deeper investment and technology collaboration with Karnataka
articles.summary: UAE Ambassador Abdulla Saif Al Nuaimi met with Karnataka leaders during the Bengaluru Tech Summit to discuss AI, startups, and urban infrastructure. The UAE proposed connecting Indian startups with Middle Eastern investors and developing AI-driven public service solutions. Talks also covered healthcare and medical education skills development.

articles.headline: Nilekani panel considers normalising school board marks for competitive entrance exams
articles.summary: A high-powered task force led by Nandan Nilekani is reviewing suggestions to give greater weightage to school board marks in entrance exams like JEE. Over 54,000 suggestions have been received. The challenge remains normalising scores across different state boards to ensure fairness, a practice previously scrapped in 2017 due to anomalies.

articles.headline: Government attempts to resolve protests against 11,000MW Siang hydropower project
articles.summary: The Arunachal Pradesh government is seeking dialogue with protesters opposing the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. The 11,000MW dam is considered strategic due to Chinese dam construction upstream. Authorities promised to protect indigenous heritage and provide adequate compensation while stressing the project's national importance.

articles.headline: Chief Justice urges citizens to respect constitutional institutions while criticising rulings
articles.summary: Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant advised that while citizens have the right to disagree with judicial decisions, they should avoid targeting the institutions themselves. Speaking in Shimla, he noted that personal attacks on institutions risk undermining public confidence essential for a functioning democracy.

articles.headline: Dhirendra Shastri’s religious tours gain political significance ahead of 2027 polls
articles.summary: Popular preacher Dhirendra Shastri of Bageshwar Dham is conducting events in Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, drawing significant political attendance. Leaders from BJP and AAP are engaging with the "kathas" to connect with large audiences. Shastri’s rhetoric on Hindu unity and specific religious sites align with upcoming election agendas in both states.

articles.headline: Marico imposes three lakh rupee penalty on director for insider trading
articles.summary: FMCG major Marico has fined independent director Bhaskar Bhat ₹3 lakh after his spouse purchased 200 equity shares during a prohibited trading period. The trade occurred on November 8, 2026, with a value of ₹1.79 lakh. The penalty was reported in a regulatory filing as a violation of the company's internal code of conduct.

articles.headline: New IBBI rules allow project-specific insolvency proceedings for real estate
articles.summary: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India has introduced amendments allowing the exclusion of viable or completed projects from a developer's corporate insolvency process. The move requires the appointment of professionals to assess each project individually. It aims to protect homebuyers and ensure stalled projects are resolved without affecting healthy ones.

articles.headline: Some Tata trustees oppose using charitable funds for Tata Sons legal battle
articles.summary: Internal friction has emerged within Tata Trusts over chairman Noel Tata’s plan to use philanthropic resources to fund legal disputes with Tata Sons. Opposing trustees argue that funds are meant for charity and not corporate litigation. They are seeking case-by-case approval for legal expenditures rather than a blanket authorization.

articles.headline: JioStar appoints Bharath Ram as Chief Operating Officer for digital business
articles.summary: Media joint venture JioStar has elevated Bharath Ram to the position of COO, Digital. In his new role, Ram will oversee outcomes for both the entertainment and sports segments. He will report to Ishan Chatterjee, with a dotted-line relationship to vice-chairperson Uday Shankar. The appointment is effective immediately.

articles.headline: Dr Devi Shetty urges government to scrap 18 percent GST on group health cover
articles.summary: Narayana Health founder Dr. Devi Shetty has called for the removal of GST on group health insurance to make medical cover affordable for the working class. He argued that the current tax makes it difficult to provide low-cost policies for gig workers. Shetty believes India can become the first country to dissociate healthcare from personal wealth.

articles.headline: Kolkata emerges as major hub for Global Capability Centres with high growth
articles.summary: Kolkata recorded a 239% year-on-year growth in office leasing for Global Capability Centres (GCCs). Multi-nationals are attracted to the city’s lower operating costs and talent pool from institutions like IIT Kharagpur and IIM Calcutta. The West Bengal government’s 2026 Investment Promotion Policy offers incentives of up to 120% of capital investment.

articles.headline: Asian regulators launch intervention measures to halt stock market decline
articles.summary: Regulators in China, South Korea, and Taiwan have introduced measures to stabilize markets following a slump in US equities. China eased margin requirements for investors, which could release $60 billion in funds. South Korea announced phased support to calm volatility, while Taiwan implemented intervention steps to restore investor confidence.

articles.headline: Government bond yield curve flattens amid cooling oil prices and inflation
articles.summary: The yield curve on Indian government bonds has flattened as investors expect a lower terminal interest rate. SBI revised its December rate hike projection from 50 to 25 basis points due to moderating crude oil prices. Corporate bond curves have also inverted, reflecting a shift in market expectations for future monetary tightening and inflation.

articles.headline: Foreign investor sentiment flips as FPIs pump 1.18 lakh crore into India
articles.summary: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have turned net buyers for 13 consecutive sessions in November, investing ₹1.18 lakh crore. This marks a sharp reversal from two years of selling. The current pace of buying is equivalent to ₹1,450 crore per trading hour, signaling renewed global interest in Indian equities following a prolonged selloff.

articles.headline: Housing finance companies cut interest rates to prevent borrower migration
articles.summary: Lenders like Home First Finance and India Shelter Finance are offering interest rate concessions and top-up loans to retain customers. The move aims to lower balance-transfer outflows as competition from banks intensifies. Aadhar Housing Finance reported a reduction in customer exits to 5.1% through data-driven retention strategies.

articles.headline: Indian GCCs become global cybersecurity hubs for major international banks
articles.summary: Global financial giants like JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs are housing critical cybersecurity operations in India. Nearly half of firms with cybersecurity Global Capability Centres (GCCs) now have their global teams reporting to India-based leaders. These centers focus on threat intelligence, cloud security, and mitigating AI-driven vulnerabilities.

articles.headline: Electric two-wheeler makers expand retail networks to challenge legacy manufacturers
articles.summary: Electric vehicle startups like Ather Energy, Oben Electric, and Ultraviolette are aggressively expanding their physical dealership networks across India. The shift marks a transition from direct-to-consumer models to deep distribution to build scale. Ola Electric aims for 700 stores by March 2027 to compete with established giants like TVS and Hero.

articles.headline: Hexaware CEO Vivek Jetley initiates 90-day review to focus on AI
articles.summary: Hexaware’s new CEO, Vivek Jetley, has launched a 90-day strategic review to prioritize AI-driven growth and big-ticket deals. Backed by Carlyle, the company is targeting niche acquisitions in data modernization and cybersecurity. Jetley aims to increase market share in non-US geographies like Europe and Canada while leveraging the parent's network.

articles.headline: Subroto Bagchi urges gig platforms to focus on worker welfare and prosperity
articles.summary: Mindtree cofounder Subroto Bagchi has called for gig platforms like Zomato and Swiggy to align their high valuations with improved working conditions for delivery riders. As chairman of the Karnataka Skill Development Vision Group, he criticized the "rag-tag" conditions of workers and urged a shift toward technical training over traditional degrees.

articles.headline: Indian telecom operators report network resilience against AI-driven cyberattacks
articles.summary: Government-ordered audits of Indian telecom networks, including Jio and Airtel, have found no major vulnerabilities to AI-driven cyberthreats. The assessment followed the launch of advanced AI models like Claude Mythos. Operators are now deploying AI-aided monitoring systems ahead of new Trai rules requiring board-approved AI governance policies.

articles.headline: Industry flags land and power gaps in Karnataka data centre policy
articles.summary: Data centre operators have expressed concerns that Karnataka’s new policy excludes projects within Bengaluru from direct land and power subsidies. The government aims for 1,000 MW capacity by 2031 but faces pushback over the lack of incentives for urban locations. Firms like Sify and Yotta are seeking competitive power costs to attract investment.

articles.headline: OpenAI upgrades security to prevent unauthorized extraction of model reasoning
articles.summary: OpenAI has implemented new safeguards to stop attackers from stealing internal reasoning processes from its AI models. The company reported that the success rate for such "adversarial distillation" attacks fell to 0.2% in its latest GPT updates. The move aims to protect intellectual property and maintain competitive advantage in AI development.

articles.headline: CrowdStrike considers acquisition of cybersecurity rival Zscaler
articles.summary: Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike is reportedly in discussions to acquire rival Zscaler. Zscaler, valued at approximately $32 billion, saw its shares rise 17% following reports of the potential deal. If completed, the merger would create one of the world's largest pure-play cybersecurity providers, signaling further consolidation in the software sector.

articles.headline: YouTube reaches three billion dollar settlement over platform addiction claims
articles.summary: YouTube has reached an in-principle agreement to pay $3 billion to settle lawsuits from US school districts. The districts accused the platform of designing addictive features that harmed students' mental health. The settlement includes new product safeguards for teenagers and requires approval from a California federal judge.

articles.headline: AI startup Cognition AI seeks funding at 75 billion dollar valuation
articles.summary: Coding assistant startup Cognition AI is in talks to raise over $2 billion at a staggering $75 billion valuation. The funding round comes just two months after its previous capital raise. The company has already raised more than $3 billion in 2026, reflecting intense investor interest in specialized artificial intelligence development tools.

articles.headline: Oracle secures funding for major infrastructure contract with OpenAI
articles.summary: Oracle has confirmed it has the necessary capital to fulfill its infrastructure deal with OpenAI. The company expects the contract to generate over $20 billion in cash flow by 2029. Oracle stated its recent capital raise makes it the first hyperscaler to be fully funded for its current investment cycle, addressing investor concerns over financing costs.

articles.headline: Nepal PM Balendra Shah Begins India Visit for Key Bilateral Talks
articles.summary: Nepal PM Balendra Shah (Balen Shah) began his first official India visit Sunday in New Delhi. Talks with PM Modi will deepen cooperation in energy, connectivity, infrastructure, hydropower, resource development, and digital payments. Agendas include climate change, Pancheshwar Multipurpose Project, Dharchula Bridge, and a new train link. Multiple agreements are expected during the multi-day tour to reset bilateral ties.

articles.headline: COP31 Climate Summit Fails Over Fossil Fuel Phase-Out Language
articles.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, ended without a deal after negotiators failed to agree on fossil fuel language, particularly a phase-out. Saudi Arabia and other oil producers blocked mentions, while over 130 nations led by the EU rejected the draft. India, China, and Saudi Arabia supported the text, stressing nationally determined transitions. The longest-ever session also lacked consensus on climate finance.

articles.headline: SP, Congress Start Seat-Sharing Talks for 2027 UP Elections
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress began formal seat-sharing talks in New Delhi for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. SP formed a four-member committee led by Ram Gopal Yadav. Congress seeks a "respectable" deal, aiming to unite against the BJP. Discussions will focus on winnability and social equations, with Congress highlighting alleged temple donation irregularities.

articles.headline: FSSAI Prosecutes Bisleri Over Unsafe Packaged Water Samples
articles.summary: FSSAI has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after samples of its packaged drinking water were found "unsafe." The water exceeded permissible bromate limits and contained polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), violating the FSS Act, 2006. Bisleri contested findings, but a second lab confirmed them. FSSAI also suspended Urmi Lifesciences and Gaur Ayurvedic Store licenses.

articles.headline: Amit Shah: Northeast Transformed, Border Villages See Reverse Migration
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah stated the Northeast has seen massive infrastructure and security transformation over 12 years, crediting PM Modi's 'Act East' policy for ending insurgency and boosting connectivity. In Arunachal Pradesh, he highlighted that the Vibrant Villages Programme, with projects worth over ₹5,610 crore, led to reverse migration in border villages, making their development a national priority.

articles.headline: Nine Pilgrims Die in Rajasthan Road Accident; SUV Driver Suspected Asleep
articles.summary: Nine Maharashtra family members, including four women and two girls, died in a tragic road accident in Kota, Rajasthan, when their SUV collided with a parked truck. They were returning from Khatu Shyam temple. Eight others were injured. Police suspect the SUV driver dozed off and booked the truck driver for illegal parking. Maharashtra government announced aid.

articles.headline: Tata Steel to Sell Tubes & Colors Businesses to APL Apollo for ₹28,000 Cr
articles.summary: Tata Steel will sell its tubes business and 100% stake in Tata Steel Colors (formerly Tata BlueScope Steel) to APL Apollo Tubes for ₹28,000 crore. The tubes unit (including Jamshedpur & Hosur facilities) is valued at up to ₹11,700 crore, and the Colors business at ₹16,300 crore. This strategic move aims to rationalize downstream portfolios, with transactions inter-conditional and targeting March 2028 completion, pending approvals.

articles.headline: India's Net Oil & Gas Import Bill Jumps 60% to $16 Billion in October
articles.summary: India's net oil and gas import bill surged 60% year-on-year to $16 billion in October 2026, primarily due to Brent crude averaging $124.77 per barrel, despite only 11% import volume rise. Crude imports cost $19.5 billion, with petroleum product exports at $6.3 billion. The April-October net bill hit $97.7 billion, pressuring trade deficit and current account.

articles.headline: Verstappen Wins Thrilling Las Vegas GP, His 75th Career F1 Victory
articles.summary: Max Verstappen won his 75th career victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, his second consecutive win there, after a thrilling race with 35 lead changes and 352 overtakes. The Red Bull driver, starting from pole, held off McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. The event, which saw Ferrari teammates Leclerc and Hamilton collide, bolstered Verstappen's 2026 F1 Championship position despite track criticism.

articles.headline: Pant's Record 128 Powers India to Highest Away Test Total
articles.summary: Rishabh Pant's aggressive 128, his ninth Test century, powered India to a record-breaking 720/9 declared against New Zealand in Wellington, India's highest-ever away Test total. With Dhruv Jurel contributing 78, India secured a 352-run lead. Pant, the first Asian wicketkeeper with centuries in AUS, ENG, SA, NZ, hit nine sixes, becoming Test cricket's second-highest six-hitter.

articles.headline: China's Secret Group Smuggles Advanced AI Chips, Bypassing Western Curbs
articles.summary: A New York Times report reveals China's Ministry of State Security, led by Chen Yixin, has run a two-year campaign to smuggle advanced semiconductor/AI chips. This secret working group uses front companies to bypass Western export restrictions, acquire hardware, and gather intelligence on the global supply chain, with about $3.6 billion in government funds flowing to linked entities.

articles.headline: GTA VI Launch Breaks Sales Records, ISPs Manage Massive Traffic Spikes
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI's launch generated $3.8 billion in first-day sales, causing a 31% surge in US internet traffic and 200GB downloads. Indian ISPs successfully managed massive data spikes using cricket-event strategies like CDNs and preloading. The game, set in Leonida with protagonists Jason and Lucia, is lauded for its storytelling. India's gaming market reached ₹14,344 crore with 535 million gamers.

articles.headline: JK Urbanscapes to Invest ₹965 Cr in 6 Non-Metro Hotels, 650 Keys
articles.summary: JK Urbanscapes Developers, part of the JK Organisation, will invest ₹965 crore in India's hospitality sector, adding 650 keys across six non-metro Tier-II cities like Bodh Gaya, Mussoorie, and Kanpur. The investment, targeting religious and leisure tourism, involves partnerships with operators like IHCL (Taj) and Minor Hotels, with the first IHCL SeleQtions hotel in Bodh Gaya opening early next year.

articles.headline: Maruti Suzuki Hikes Select Vehicle Prices by 0.31% Amid Cost Pressures
articles.summary: Maruti Suzuki India announced a volume-weighted average price hike of 0.31% across select vehicle models, effective November 22, 2026. This fourth price increase in the current financial year is attributed to sustained cost pressures, despite internal cost-reduction efforts, and follows a nearly 26% decline in the company's consolidated net profit.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu Seeks SC Review on Karthigai Deepam Lamp Ritual Order
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government filed a review petition in the Supreme Court challenging its order permitting the Karthigai Deepam lamp ritual at Thiruparankundram hill. The disputed site, contested by Hindu worshippers and a dargah, was allowed for a one-time lighting on November 24 by authorized officials without public congregation, but the state's religious endowments department is contesting operational details.

articles.headline: Tata Sons Board to Decide on ₹18 Lakh Cr IPO Amid RBI Mandate
articles.summary: Tata Sons' board will meet on November 26 to decide on a public listing, mandated by the RBI for upper-layer NBFCs. Chairman N Chandrasekaran pushes for an IPO, rejecting Noel Tata's restructuring proposal to remain private. Non-compliance could bring civil/criminal implications; RBI rejected a 2024 deregistration. The listing could value the company at ₹18 lakh crore, following a postponed meeting.

articles.headline: Arunachal Border Villages See Reverse Migration Due to VVP: Amit Shah
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced that 40 villages along Arunachal Pradesh's China border are seeing residents return due to the Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP). Shah inaugurated ₹5,610 crore worth of VVP projects, providing improved infrastructure, electricity, and healthcare to make border areas self-sufficient. Arunachal Pradesh received ₹1.49 lakh crore in central aid between 2014-2024.

articles.headline: Nirmala Sitharaman: 50 Crore Indians Lifted from Poverty in Decade
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that 50 crore (500 million) Indians escaped poverty between 2011 and 2023. She attributed this to government schemes like Jan Dhan, DBT, PM Awas Yojana, Swachh Bharat, and Jal Jeevan Mission, which addressed household deprivations and fostered financial inclusion. Sitharaman emphasized extreme poverty is almost eradicated, shifting focus to wider inclusion.

articles.headline: ED Chargesheets Widespread KPSC Paper Leak, Bribery for Jobs
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate filed a chargesheet in the KPSC examination scam, exposing widespread paper leaks and bribery. The probe under PMLA revealed senior officials and relatives took payments, including ₹2 crore for interview marks for daughters, to secure jobs. Proceeds were allegedly used for cash, jewelry, luxury items, and travel, highlighting massive irregularities in recruitment.

articles.headline: India-China Military Talks Conclude, Reportedly Ease Eastern LAC Tensions
articles.summary: Indian and Chinese military commanders concluded their second 10-day talks, focusing on easing tensions along the eastern LAC in Arunachal Pradesh. Led by Lt. Gen. Girish Kalia, the Indian side discussed winter face-off protocols. Sources report visible de-escalation, following renewed diplomatic efforts and high-level engagements between NSA Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi to resolve the border dispute.

articles.headline: SCO Forum Adopts 'Indraprastha Communiqué' for Cultural Heritage Preservation
articles.summary: The SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi adopted the 'Indraprastha Communiqué,' a charter recognizing culture as a friendship bridge. It calls for collaborative UNESCO heritage nominations and joint action against trafficking, with member states agreeing to use AI for heritage access and preservation. Delegates, including from Pakistan, attended the three-day event, proposing a digital repository for shared traditions.

articles.headline: CAQM Report: Delhi Misses Landfill Targets, Punjab/Haryana Lag in Stubble Management
articles.summary: A CAQM report revealed Delhi missed targets for clearing 52.7 lakh metric tonnes of legacy waste at its three major landfills, with Ghazipur showing slowest progress (16.53%). Meanwhile, Punjab and Haryana met only 53% and 35% of industrial paddy straw utilization targets due to bottlenecks in processing plants and green crematoriums. Municipal waste processing also remains behind schedule.

articles.headline: Government Launches New Education & Social Welfare Initiatives
articles.summary: The government launched new initiatives and a social welfare scheme aimed at improving literacy rates and enhancing access to quality education for underprivileged communities. These programs are designed to provide targeted assistance to vulnerable populations, thereby improving living standards and promoting social equity.
